newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends broadly up after late buying spree.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends broadly up after late buying spree.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed broadly higher in a late, technical buying spree that was initiated by some commission houses, traders said.

KCBT wheat was higher all day on feelings that wheat had been oversold Friday. Support also came from a lack of selling and renewed bullishness about USDA's Friday crop report, which trimmed the estimate for U.S. wheat production.
"Wheat's divorcing itself from the overall influence of beans," a trader said at the midsession. "The bottom line is that Friday's report was friendly for wheat."
KCBT wheat closed one to nine cents per bushel higher, with Dec up nine cents at $4.44-1/2. March gained 7-1/2 cents to close at $4.24-1/2.

Traders said Refco and Wolcott Lincoln bought after stops were hit toward the close. Rosenthal Collins also bought at the close after having been an aggressive buyer throughout the session, they said.
The players' sheet showed Rosenthal bought 2.6 million Dec bushels. CIS sold 1.1 million Dec. Man International bull-spread 900,000 Dec/March at 19-1/2 to 21 cents.
Some traders noted that the December/December spread with CBOT wheat may have closed out of line Monday, hinting that KCBT Dec could weaken relative to CBOT Dec on Tuesday.
